scenes.headline: How ten agents share one decision call
scenes.sub: One shared state, ten questions, and a resolver in code.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tangerine! A swarm of agents can ask a decision model everything in one call. Here's how, and where the teamwork really lives.

scenes.text: The expensive half of a decision is the state. Ten agents looking at one world send ten questions against one copy of it.

steps.say: Ten snakes share one arena. Before anything is asked, code measures every move: food distance, reachable cells, dead-end risk.
Each tick sends one request: the state once, plus ten short questions. Ten answers come back in roughly the time of one.

steps.note: Intentions stay private: no question sees another's answer
steps.say: Each snake gets its own probabilities. By design, no question can see another's answer.
So coordination happens in code: a resolver enumerates joint moves, drops illegal ones, and keeps the likeliest, in about half a millisecond.

steps.note: Override rate in the published run: 2.2%
steps.say: How often it overrules the model is the honest diagnostic.

scenes.title: A live tick, in the project's app

steps.say: A live tick in the project's own app. Four snakes are still alive, and four questions went in one request.
This tick's decisions: each snake gets its own move, with its own probability.
And the override rate the README calls its Go or No-Go gate: two point two percent.

left.title: Choice readout
left.say: Grouped against one shared state, the choice readout barely moved: two hundred sixty-nine of two hundred seventy answers agreed.

right.title: Score readout
items: Reports where the mass sits on a rubric
Shifted about 0.29 levels, on a 0 to 3 scale
right.say: The score readout, a weighted mean over a rubric, shifted about zero point two nine levels. The winner survives a shift that a mean does not.

scenes.text: A batch shares the state, not the answers: coordination is code, and only the score readout shows the drift.
scenes.mark: shares the state, not the answers

recap: One request: one shared state, ten questions
Coordination is a resolver in code, not the model
Batching shifts scores even when choices hold
scenes.say: To recap: share the state, resolve in code, and check the scores.
